analysis.title: US midterm elections' impact on the health care sector
key_insights: UBS CIO's Eric Potoker says the 2026 US midterm outcome was broadly in line with market expectations (Democrats won the House and the Senate), but the margin of the Democratic win exceeded expectations and was likely at the extreme end of the scenarios investors had considered.

Democrats had secured 54 Senate seats as of Thursday's open after the election (52 Democrats plus two independents who caucus with them). The Mississippi and Alaska Senate races remain too close to call.

Democratic Senate wins in Texas, South Carolina and Kansas are the first in those states in multiple decades. UBS says they raise the prospect of a political shift that could continue into the 2028 cycle and make larger health care policy changes more likely after 2028.

UBS expects policy gridlock to be the most likely outcome in the next Congress and thinks investors already expected it. It does not expect significant health care policy changes in 2027-28, and it thinks President Trump would likely veto major health care legislation sponsored by congressional Democrats.

UBS sees some modest expansion of government-sponsored health insurance coverage as more likely, in the lame-duck session or the next Congress. It sees potential for Medicaid relief, which would be a modest positive for the sector overall.

UBS thinks the direction of investor sentiment toward health care policy risk is negatively skewed. Investors have held a benign view of this risk over the past year, leaving little room for sentiment to become more benign.

Pharmaceutical and managed care stocks are the sectors UBS sees as vulnerable if policy fears rise. Democrats will likely raise major insurance reform, including Medicare for All, which UBS thinks is unlikely to pass but could add uncertainty for managed care. Democrats will also likely focus on drug pricing regulation, which would weigh on pharma sentiment.

Medical device and life sciences tools (LST) stocks have often been favored in past periods of health care policy uncertainty, and UBS expects a similar relative preference if policy fears grow over the next two years.

Health care providers, including hospital management companies, typically perform well when policymakers pursue expanded insurance coverage. Near-term Medicaid expansion or a reduction to upcoming cuts would be positive for providers and for device companies that sell to hospitals.

UBS thinks the 2028 election is distant and uncertain and may not weigh heavily on health care stocks near term. As the election nears and candidates and platforms become clearer, it thinks health care valuations could become more vulnerable.

risk_factors: Rising health care policy uncertainty ahead of the 2028 presidential election could hurt investor sentiment and valuations.
Democratic proposals on major insurance reform, including Medicare for All, could weigh on managed care.
Democratic focus on drug pricing regulation could weigh on pharmaceutical sentiment.
A continued political shift toward Democrats in states such as Texas, South Carolina and Kansas could raise the odds of larger policy changes after 2028.
vol_and_positioning: Investors have held a benign view of health care policy risk over the past year, and UBS sees little room for sentiment to become more benign.
geopolitical: 2026 US midterm elections: Democrats won the House and the Senate, with a margin larger than expected.
Potential Trump veto of major health care legislation from a Democratic Congress.

key_data_points.metric: Democratic-aligned US Senate seats secured as of Thursday's open after the election (52 Democrats plus two independents)
key_data_points.context: Mississippi and Alaska races remained too close to call as of Thursday's open after the election.
key_data_points.anchor: Democrats have secured 54 Senate seats (52 Democrats plus two independents who caucus with Democrats)

tension_points.bull_case: Gridlock through 2028 means Democratic control has no significant effect on health care company growth outlooks, and some Medicaid relief would be a modest positive for the sector.
tension_points.bear_case: The size of the Democratic win raises the odds of larger health policy changes after the 2028 election, including drug pricing and insurance reform, which would hurt sentiment and valuations for pharma and managed care.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A major health care bill from congressional Democrats that Trump does not veto would invalidate the gridlock view. UBS also expects valuation vulnerability to grow as 2028 candidates and platforms become clearer.

theme_stances.key_argument: Near-term policy impact is small because of gridlock, but a larger Democratic win raises the odds of policy change after 2028 and could hurt sentiment and valuations.
theme_stances.evidence: Near term we see little impact, but with the prospect for rising investor anxiety
